BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. Iq s. 204_ HON. EMMYLOU J. TALINO-MENDOZA Provincial Capitol Amas, Kidapawan City Cotabato Dear Governor Mendoza: FEB 142025 This has reference to your Letter dated January 2, 2025, concerning the application for terminal benefits of former Governor Nancy A. Catamco of Cotabato Province. At the outset, this Department is of the submission that the Secretaryäf the Interior and Local Government (SILG) is not the proper approving authority for terminal leave application benefits of local elective officials. While it is true that the SILG is the approving authority for leave of absences for governors pursuant to Section 47(a)(1) of the Local Government Code in relation to Administrative Order No. 267, 19921, such authority, however, does not extend to approving their terminal leave benefits. Here, it bears noting that leave of absence under Section 47 of the Code contemplates a temporary non-performance of duties and functions of local elective officials. Terminal leave, on the other hand, refers to the money value of the total accumulated leave credits of an employee based on the highest salary rate received prior to or upon the retirement date/voluntary separation2. The Omnibus Rules on Leave issued by the Civil Service Commission (CSC)3 set forth the guidelines and parameters on the application for terminal leave. In particular, Sections 35 to 37 of the said Rules provide, thus: "Section. 35. Terminal leave. — Terminal leave is applied for by an official or an employee who intends to sever his connection with his employer. Accordingly, the filing of application for terminal leave requires as a condition sine qua non, the employee's resignation, retirement or separation from the service without any fault on his part. It must be shown first that public employment cease by any of the said modes of severances. "Delegating Certain General Supervisory Powers of the President Over Local Governments to the Secretary of Interior and Local Government." 2 Rule I (12), CSC Memorandum Circular No. 41, s. 1998, titled "Amendments to Rules I and XVI Of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of the Administrative Code of 1987 (Executive Order 292). 3 Ibid "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Section 36. Approval of terminal leave. — Application for commutation of vacation and sick leave in connection with separation through no fault of an official or employee shall be sent to the head of department concerned for approval. In this connection, clearance from the Ombudsman is no longer required for processing and payment of terminal leave as such clearance is needed for payment of retirement benefits. Section 37. Payment of terminal leave. — Any official/employee of the government who retires, voluntarily resigns, so is separated from the service through no fault of his own, and who is not otherwise covered by special law, shall be entitled to the commutation of his leave credits exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays without limitation and regardless of the period when the credits were earned." Accordingly, the application for commutation of terminal leave shall be made with the head of the department (i.e., the Human Resources department) concerned. Stated differently, the application for terminal leave benefits of local elective officials should be processed within the LGU's concerned office, subject to pertinent rules and regulations issued by CSC, the Department of Budget and Management4, and the Commission on Audit. Notwithstanding, please note that this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/jam DEBIE T.
